speaker: otto
text: わしは灯台守のオットー。\n灯台の火が消えてしまって、\nゆうべは眠れんかった。
direction: first meeting; tired and worried, a sleepless old man introducing himself with a heavy sigh

speaker: otto
text: ……なに、灯台へ行くと？\nひとりで？ とんでもない。\n酒場「潮風亭」で仲間を見つけておいで。
direction: surprised, then protective and scolding like a grandfather; firm but kind at the end

speaker: otto
text: おお、仲間を連れてきたか。\nそれなら話は別じゃ。
direction: pleasantly surprised, relieved, a warm chuckle in the voice

speaker: otto
text: 灯台の守り歌が、\nどうしても思い出せんのじゃ。\nあの歌がなけりゃ、火はつかん。
direction: quietly distressed, ashamed that his memory fails him; slow

speaker: otto
text: ……頼む。\nこれが灯台の鍵じゃ。
direction: a heartfelt plea after a pause, handing over something precious; low and sincere

speaker: otto
text: 灯台は、町を出て南の\n岬の先じゃ。行く前に、\n戦いの心得を教えておこう。
direction: practical and steady, an old hand giving directions, a little proud to teach

speaker: otto
text: 中から、ネズミの鳴き声が……\n気をつけるんじゃ！
direction: hushed alarm, listening at the door, then a sharp warning

speaker: otto
text: ……危なかったのう。\nひと息ついて、もう一度じゃ。
direction: relieved and encouraging, gentle

speaker: otto
text: 今のは……『閃き』じゃな。\n戦いの中で、ふいに\n新しい技を思いつくことがある。
direction: impressed and delighted, an old man recognising something he has seen before

speaker: otto
text: 今のは……『閃き』じゃな。\n戦いの中で、ふいに\n新しい術を思いつくことがある。
direction: impressed and delighted, an old man recognising something he has seen before

speaker: otto
text: わしは港へ戻っておる。\n上の灯室を、頼んだぞ。
direction: trusting, entrusting the task; warm and firm

speaker: otto
text: ♪　海の果てまで、灯よ届け\n帰る舟に、道を照らせ……。
direction: he half-sings, half-hums the old lighthouse song he just got back, slow and a little shaky, full of emotion; a plain folk melody, not performed

speaker: otto
text: これは、わしが若いころから\n使ってきたランタンじゃ。\n持っていっておくれ。
direction: tender and grateful, giving a treasured keepsake

speaker: otto
text: 若いころ、灯台には\n『朝番』というのがあってな。\n火が戻ったら、また立てるつもりじゃ。
direction: fond reminiscence, smiling, looking forward

speaker: otto
text: ……はて。何を見張る番\nじゃったかのう。\nどうしても思い出せん。
direction: the smile fades into puzzlement; quiet, a little lost, unsettling in its gentleness

speaker: berna
text: そうそう、大事な話があるんだ。
direction: remembering something important, gently turning serious

speaker: berna
text: 近ごろ、あちこちで\n伝承が消えていくんだよ。
direction: worried, lowering her voice

speaker: berna
text: 歌の続きが出てこない。\n祭りの由来が分からない。\nそんな話ばかりさ。
direction: listing the signs with quiet sadness, unhurried

speaker: berna
text: わたしたち語り部は、それを\n『白紙』と呼んでいる。
direction: grave, naming something ominous with care

speaker: berna
text: 里の語り石の文字も、\n半分が白く抜けてしまった。
direction: sad, looking toward the village stone

speaker: berna
text: それにね、港町ファロスの\n灯台の火が、細りはじめて三晩。\nきのう、とうとう消えたそうだ。
direction: telling news she has heard, concern growing to the last sentence

speaker: berna
text: あの灯台には、守り歌という\n古い伝承があってね。\nそれも、白紙になりかけている。
direction: a storyteller's voice, fond of the old tale, then worried

speaker: berna
text: ただし、ひとりで行っちゃ\nだめだよ。ファロスの酒場\n「潮風亭」で、仲間を探しなさい。
direction: a mentor's gentle warning, slightly stern then warm

speaker: berna
text: それから、これを持って\nお行き。
direction: kind, handing over a small parcel

speaker: berna
text: 昔からの習わしさ。\n誰の席かは……忘れちまったよ。
direction: light and matter-of-fact at first, then a small puzzled pause; a hint of sadness she does not notice

speaker: berna
text: うわさは酒場に集まるものさ。\nまずは港の酒場で\n聞いてごらん。
direction: cheerful advice, a knowing smile

speaker: berna
text: わたしは里へ帰るよ。\n……いってらっしゃい、
direction: warm farewell; after いってらっしゃい she starts to say the apprentice's name and cannot find it: the line trails off unfinished, a tiny stall

speaker: berna
text: おかえり。年代記は、\nちゃんと書いているかい？
direction: welcoming someone home, teasing a little

speaker: berna
text: 森の灯が戻ったそうだね。\n語り石の文字が、ほんの少し\n読めるようになった気がするよ。
direction: proud and moved, quietly happy

speaker: berna
text: よく眠れたかい？\n……さあ、いってらっしゃい。
direction: soft morning voice, gentle send-off

speaker: fine
text: ……気をつけて。
direction: barely above a whisper, sincere, as she turns to go

speaker: fine
text: ……風も、歌を覚えているのね。
direction: wistful and faintly amused, like talking to herself on a windy hill

speaker: fine
text: ……ねえ、聞こえる？
direction: the opening of the game over black: an intimate whisper to the player, a voice from very far away

speaker: fine
text: これは、忘れられかけた物語。
direction: soft storyteller's narration, slow

speaker: fine
text: そして、それを語り直した、\nひとりの語り部の物語。
direction: narration, a quiet warmth and hope on the last words

speaker: rowell
text: 灯台に火が戻っただと？\n……写し取ったはずの歌が、\nどうして。
direction: stunned disbelief, then a shaken half-whisper; the first crack in his certainty

speaker: rowell
text: 灯台守から鍵を借りたそうだな。\n……火をともせるものなら、\nともしてみるがいい。
direction: cool and sarcastic, a challenge

speaker: rowell
text: まだいたのか。\n写し取った伝承は、本院で\n大切に保管される。
direction: curt and dismissive, bureaucratic pride

speaker: elm
text: 森の道は、もう閉ざさぬ。\n夏至の歌も、村の者たちが\nまた歌ってくれるだろう。
direction: calm and grateful, slow and resonant

speaker: elm
text: ただ、迷いの森の魔物は、\nわたしにも鎮められぬ。\n腕を磨くには、よいだろう。
direction: wise, a faint dry humour at the end

speaker: tadeo
text: よい灯りを。
direction: the world's everyday greeting in the endless night; a businesslike oil merchant, friendly, brief

speaker: fishwife
text: よい灯りを。
direction: brisk, cheerful harbour woman greeting a passer-by

speaker: gateguard
text: よい灯りを、旅の方。
direction: a town gate guard, polite and a bit formal

speaker: master
text: いらっしゃい。
direction: a tavern keeper welcoming a guest, warm and easygoing

speaker: gord
text: おう、あんたか。
direction: a gruff woodcutter chief, tired but glad to see someone

speaker: hanna
text: おや、旅の方。
direction: a kind old village woman, gentle surprise

speaker: rita
text: あ、語り部さん。
direction: a young village singer, clear and bright, a little shy

speaker: pim
key: bark: when the talk opens (after the rescue)
text: あっ、語り部さん！
direction: a ten-year-old boy, excited and happy

speaker: fine
key: caption after 「……ねえ、聞こえる？」 (the lighthouse song over black; ev.caption voice)
text: ♪　海の果てまで、灯よ届け\n帰る舟に、道を照らせ
direction: the very start of the game, over black: she softly sings-speaks the old lighthouse lullaby like someone rocking a cradle, very slow, a gentle rise and fall on each phrase, a long tender pause between the two lines, warm and hushed; a plain chanted folk lullaby, not a performed song

speaker: fine
key: caption after the Page Eater (the song comes back on the paper; ev.caption voice)
text: ♪　海の果てまで、灯よ届け\n帰る舟に、道を照らせ
direction: the lost words slowly reappear on a slip of paper and she reads the lighthouse song back to life as a lullaby: slow chant-like cadence, soft wonder and quiet relief, each phrase lingering and fading, hushed like singing a child to sleep; not a performed song

speaker: berna
key: E.say after ev.createHero (the name shows first; the voice skips {hero})
text: ……うん、いい名前だ。
direction: after hearing the new apprentice's name: a short, clear, affirmative nod-word うん (yes — not a hesitant hmm), then warm fond approval like a grandmother, a small smile in the voice

speaker: berna
key: P2[7] (the name shows first; the voice skips {hero})
text: 行っておくれ。\n語り部の見習いとしての、\n最初の仕事だよ。
direction: sending her apprentice off on the first real job: gentle but firm, proud and a little moved, unhurried

speaker: otto
key: first time say 1 (the name shows first; the voice skips {hero})
text: 灯台に火が戻ったぞ！\n守り歌も、思い出せた。
direction: overjoyed and moved, an old man almost laughing with relief; the lighthouse is lit again and the song came back

speaker: rita
key: first talk page 1 (sings the first verse, then stops)
text: ♪　眠れ森の主、千の年輪に……。\nだめ。この先が、\nどうしても出てこないの。
direction: sings the first line softly and slowly as a melody, then breaks off; frustrated and sad that the rest will not come

speaker: rita
text: わたしはリタ。この村の歌い手。\n千年樹の歌は、最初の一節しか\n思い出せないの。
direction: introduces herself shyly and earnestly; a little ashamed that the village singer has forgotten the song

speaker: rita
key: the song night in the plaza (before the song)
text: みんな、聞いて。\n千年樹の歌よ。
direction: calls the gathered village to listen, happy and a little nervous; she can sing the whole song again

speaker: zaid
text: わしは隊商の長ザイード。\n掲示を見てくれたか。
direction: first meeting; introduces himself plainly, a caravan master sizing up the travellers

speaker: zaid
text: 王墓のオアシスへ、供え物を運ぶ。\n昔からの習わしでな。泉の水の源が、\nそこの古い泉なんだ。
direction: explains the old custom calmly, with quiet respect for the tradition

speaker: zaid
text: 砂嵐と盗賊で、隊が出せずにいる。\n護衛を頼めないか。\n野営を三晩、オアシスまでだ。
direction: worried but steady; asks for help as a serious request

speaker: zaid
text: 地の果ての、白む星……。\n祖母は、あれを「夜明けの星」と\n呼んでいた。
direction: at the campfire, looking at a star low on the horizon; soft and nostalgic, remembering his grandmother

speaker: zaid
text: ……夜明け。\nふしぎな言葉だな。\n夜が、明ける？　何が明けるんだ？
direction: puzzled and wondering, almost to himself; he does not know what the word dawn means

speaker: zaid
text: 泉が……泉が満ちていく！
direction: astonished, overjoyed, his voice rising as the water wells up

speaker: zaid
text: ……この光、祖母の歌の\n「夜明けの星」の色だ。
direction: hushed and moved, recognising the colour from his grandmother's song

speaker: rashid
text: 動くな。命まではもらわん。
direction: a masked bandit on a rock with bows drawn: cold, low and commanding

speaker: rashid
text: おれたちは「砂の鷹」。\n欲しいのは水だ。水がめを\n半分置いていけ。
direction: names his band and makes the demand; hard, businesslike, not cruel

speaker: rashid
text: ……いい腕だ。おれはラシード。\n昔は、日輪同盟の兵だった。
direction: beaten, kneeling, breathing hard; grudging respect as he gives his name and his past

speaker: rashid
text: 二十年前の代理試合の夜……\n歌が聞こえた。敵も味方も、\n手を止めた。
direction: quiet and faraway, remembering a night when a song stopped a battle

speaker: rashid
text: ……そのあとのことは、\nなぜか思い出せん。気づけば、\n砂の上で盗賊をしていた。
direction: troubled and bitter; he cannot remember what came after

speaker: rashid
text: 行け。おれたちは台地の洞へ帰る。\n……次は、こうはいかんぞ。
direction: gets up and leaves; gruff warning with a trace of respect

speaker: rashid
text: ……来たか。隊商の犬め。\nここは、おれたちの最後の巣だ。
direction: in his last hideout, hostile and cornered; spits the insult

speaker: rashid
text: 今度は、手加減せんぞ！
direction: draws his blade, fierce battle resolve

speaker: rashid
text: ……まいった。\nおれたちの負けだ。
direction: defeated and out of breath; admits it plainly

speaker: rashid
text: この手袋を持っていけ。\n……もう、盗みはやめる。\n洞の者を食わせる道を探すさ。
direction: hands over his gloves; tired, resolved to give up stealing, quietly decent

speaker: hazal
text: 水と引き換えに、わたしは名を\n砂の精霊に差し出した。
direction: the king with his name back: slow, grave, confessing an old bargain

speaker: hazal
text: 名を呼ぶかぎり、日輪の火は消えぬ。\n……その約束も、石から写されて\n消えてしまったのだ。
direction: sorrowful: the promise was copied from the stone and lost

speaker: hazal
text: 語り部よ。\nわたしの名を、もう一度\n泉の民に返してくれ。
direction: a solemn, gentle plea to the storyteller

speaker: nadia
text: わたしはナディア。踊り子よ。\n毎晩、広場で王さまの歌を\n歌って踊るの。聞いて。
direction: bright and friendly, introduces herself and invites them to listen

speaker: nadia
text: ……名前の所だけ、\nどうしても歌えないの。\n母さんも、おばあちゃんも。
direction: sad and a little embarrassed; the name will not come to anyone

speaker: nadia
text: 王さまの名前、王墓の石に\n刻まれてたって聞いたわ。\n誰も、読みに行けないけど。
direction: thoughtful, with a hint of longing

speaker: nadia
text: 王さまの名前、わかったんでしょう？\n……教えて。
direction: eager and hopeful, then quietly asking

speaker: nadia
text: ハザル……。うん、ぴったり。\n歌ってみるね。
direction: tries the name, delighted, then ready to sing

speaker: jorn
text: よい灯りを、旅の人。\nわしはヨルン。ユールの村長だ。
direction: first meeting; a warm, grave village chief greeting a traveller

speaker: jorn
text: 今夜は冬至。大火祭の夜だ。\n大かまどで冬至の火を燃やし、\n昔話を語って、峰へ運ぶ。
direction: explains the festival with pride and a little solemnity

speaker: jorn
text: 峰の白竜に火と物語を届け、\n竜は吹雪を鎮める。\n……それが村と竜の約束だ。
direction: solemn, telling the old pact between the village and the dragon

speaker: jorn
text: ところが今年は、秋から\n一日も吹雪がやまん。\n竜に物語が届いておらんのだ。
direction: worried and heavy; the blizzard has not stopped since autumn

speaker: jorn
key: the festival: asks for the tale page 1
text: 語り部よ。\n今年の物語を、火の前で\n語ってくれ。
direction: before the great fire, formal and hopeful, asking the storyteller

speaker: jorn
text: 峰の竜に届くように。
direction: quiet, a wish sent toward the peak

speaker: jorn
text: 門は三つ。北、東、西。\nわしらの手では、\n二つしか守りきれん。
direction: urgent, commanding over the howling; grim about the odds

speaker: jorn
key: the wolves page 2 (the name shows first; the voice skips {hero})
text: 力を貸してくれ。\n守る門を、選んでくれ。
direction: urgent, asking for help and trusting the storyteller

speaker: hald
text: 狼の群れだ！\n村を囲んでおる！
direction: a shouted alarm through the blizzard, urgent

speaker: hald
text: 門を閉めろ！\n男たちは門へ！
direction: shouting orders, commanding

speaker: sonja
text: ……火が細いの。\n脂を足しても、足しても。
direction: worried, murmuring by the weak fire

speaker: sonja
text: わたしはソーニャ。\n火守りの家の娘よ。\n大かまどの火を守ってるの。
direction: introduces herself quietly and earnestly

speaker: sonja
text: 祭ではね、火の前で\n物語の本を読むの。\n毎年、同じ本を。
direction: explains the custom gently

speaker: sonja
key: first talk say 2 page 2 (the blank book)
text: でも今年、本を開いたら……\n真っ白だったの。\n一文字も、残ってなかった。
direction: shaken, almost whispering; the book was completely blank

speaker: sonja
key: the square page 1 (the name shows first; the voice skips {hero})
text: おかえりなさい。
direction: relieved and happy to see them back

speaker: sonja
text: 夜数えの板に、今夜の刻みを\n入れようとしたの。\n……でも、手が止まっちゃった。
direction: thoughtful and puzzled, her hand stopped over the board

speaker: sonja
text: ……今夜は、いつもより\n空が明るい。
direction: soft wonder, looking up at a sky that is a little brighter

speaker: neve
text: ……これを持っていくがよい。\nわたしの、うろこの一枚だ。
direction: calm and gracious, the dragon giving one of her scales

speaker: mayor
key: the assembly: asks for the name
text: では、名指しを聞こう。\n子どもたちを、誰がさらった？
direction: grave, formal, chairing a tense assembly

speaker: mayor
text: 霧……だと？\n霧が、子どもをさらうというのか。
direction: taken aback, sceptical

speaker: mayor
text: 証拠を示しなさい。
direction: stern, demanding proof

speaker: mayor
text: 霧が、魔女の姿をまねて\n子どもを連れていった……。
direction: slowly realising the truth, shaken

speaker: mayor
text: ……わしらは、あやうく\n無実の館に火をかけるところだった。
direction: ashamed and relieved; the town nearly burned an innocent house

speaker: zaid
text: ♪　北のくぎ星　動かぬ星よ\n♪　迷う隊商の　くいとなれ
direction: sings a slow, simple caravan song at the campfire, low and steady, like an old folk melody

speaker: zaid
text: ♪　七つの泉星　ひしゃくを傾け\n♪　夜のしずくを　砂にまけ
direction: sings a slow, simple caravan song at the campfire, warm and steady

speaker: zaid
text: ♪　地の果ての　白む星よ\n♪　……祖母は　「夜明けの星」と呼んだ
direction: sings softly, the last line spoken more than sung, wistful

speaker: nadia
key: the king's song with the name missing (caption, X.SONG_BLANK)
text: ♪　砂の海に　水を招いた王よ\n♪　その名は――　……\n♪　夕べの祈りに　とこしえに
direction: sings a graceful dancer's song; at the missing name she falters into a silent pause, then finishes the last line

speaker: nadia
key: the king's song in full (caption, X.SONG_FULL)
text: ♪　砂の海に　水を招いた王よ\n♪　その名はハザル　日輪の友\n♪　夕べの祈りに　とこしえに
direction: sings the whole song joyfully and clearly, the name ringing out

speaker: melda
key: the bell song (caption, X.SONG, after v_melda_manor_05)
text: ♪　鳴れよ、七つの鐘\n♪　霧は沼の底へ、\n♪　朝は町の窓へ
direction: sings the old bell song softly, a ghostly lullaby
